Same unrestricted integer parity decomposition. Paired exact clients in both assistants.

Same unrestricted integer base and two nonnegative exponent premises, with multiplication on the right. Integer-power body is reviewed separately and fingerprinted here; weakening either exponent domain is not silently accepted.
Same nonnegative exponent premise. Source Z.abs_nat corresponds to Int.natAbs; negative integer powers are zero and are not absolute-exponent powers.
Same natural-exponent successor equation and unrestricted signed integer base. Lean uses ordinary Nat-indexed integer power for the source Zpower_nat.
Same positive base premise and genuine binary-positive exponent domain. Lean Zpower_pos uses its positiveToNat transport; paired typed clients check the source contract.

Same nonnegative exponent and odd-base Boolean hypotheses. The result refers to actual integer Zpower, not an absolute-exponent substitute. Paired clients reject flipping the parity hypothesis in both assistants.

Source record has an integer field with Boolean proof Z.leb 2 value = true. Lean Radix has the same integer domain with proposition proof 2 <= value. Paired clients bridge both proof presentations; Lean projections are explicit rather than source coercions. Constructor and field types are fingerprinted, not only the empty record-type hash.

Same implication from equal integer projections to equal records. Lean proof irrelevance replaces the source Boolean-equality helper without weakening admissibility.

Same valid radix and exponent-order hypothesis over all integers. Both negative powers may be zero; non-strict monotonicity still holds.

Same valid radix, nonnegative UPPER exponent and strict exponent order. Lower exponent may be negative. Both assistants prove that removing the upper-exponent premise is false using -2 < -1 but zero equal powers.

Same all-integer exponent implication from power(e1-1) < power(e2) to e1 <= e2. The reviewed direct theorem uses Zpower; the unused former check/spec wrapper had an unrelated natAbs premise and has been removed.
Same unrestricted integer index and valid radix. Negative indices are below the zero negative-power result; no natAbs exponent is substituted.

Same signed dividend, positive a and nonnegative b premises. Source floor modulo agrees with Lean Euclidean modulo on the resulting nonnegative divisor domain, including zero; paired clients and universal Lean floor/Euclidean bridges preserve that boundary.

Same unconditional nested truncating-remainder identity for all signed n,a,b, including zero factors. No spurious nonzero-divisor assumption.

Same arbitrary dividend and two nonnegative factor premises. Source floor division/modulo matches Lean Euclidean operations on these premises; zero cases retained, negative-divisor global alias explicitly rejected.
Same unconditional truncating nested-remainder/division identity for signed and zero inputs. Actual operations are tmod/tdiv, with no added positivity conditions.

Same strict |a| < b premise and remainder equal to a, with the same natAbs/absolute-value presentation bridge as the quotient law.

Same all-signed inputs, genuine 0 <= a*b hypothesis and unrestricted divisor including zero. Conclusion uses truncating quotients/remainders. Both assistants prove that the premise-free claim is false at a=-2,b=1,c=2; obsolete Euclidean check wrapper was removed.
